target_users: Ph.D. Candidates in STEM, Social Sciences, and Humanities
daily_responsibilities: Drafting and editing peer-reviewed journal manuscripts
Writing grant proposals for federal and private funding bodies (NIH, NSF, etc.)
Managing Institutional Review Board (IRB) compliance and protocol submissions
Designing and tracking experimental protocols and research methodologies
Preparing course lectures and mentoring graduate students
pain_points: Fragmented research workflows across Zotero, Word, Excel, and local folders
Lack of a centralized matrix to cross-reference literature findings with active manuscript sections
Missed grant deadlines and disorganized budget justification tracking
Difficulty tracking reviewer feedback, revision progress, and journal submission statuses
Losing track of IRB protocol expiration dates and amendment requirements
desired_outcomes: An integrated, single-workspace ecosystem connecting literature, grants, and manuscripts
Accelerated manuscript writing through structured literature synthesis matrices
Zero missed deadlines for grant applications and progress reports
Streamlined response-to-reviewers workflows to speed up acceptance rates
Seamless management of academic output metrics for annual tenure reviews
revenue_activities: Securing federal, state, and private research grants
Publishing high-impact peer-reviewed articles to maintain tenure track eligibility
Earning intellectual property royalties or patent licensing from research discoveries
Securing paid academic speaking engagements and external consulting contracts
software_currently_used: Writing Tools (Scrivener, LaTeX, Microsoft Word, Google Docs)
Data Repositories (OSF, GitHub, Box, Google Drive)
workflow_bottlenecks: The manual translation of highlighted PDF notes into structured thematic literature reviews
The disconnection between active grant aims, experimental protocols, and resulting manuscript drafts
Managing peer review revisions where reviewer comments, action plans, and manuscript changes are kept in isolated documents

existing_solution_types: Generic Notion research templates (mostly simplified reading lists)
Dedicated reference managers (Zotero, EndNote) which excel at citation but lack project planning
Academic-focused writing environments (Scrivener) lacking relational databases for compliance, grants, and IRB tracking
common_features: Basic task lists and weekly calendars
overserved_features: Basic daily task scheduling and general time-blocking
Generic 'to-do' lists unrelated to specific academic milestones
Simple, flat lists of web links labeled as 'research resources'
underserved_needs: A dynamic, relational Literature Synthesis Matrix mapping themes directly to manuscript sections
A structured Grant Pipeline tied directly to budget items, specific aims, and compliance requirements
An integrated Peer Review Response System tracking reviewer comments, planned actions, and manuscript modifications
A proactive IRB Protocol and Compliance Tracker with automated renewal warning dates
market_gaps: There is no existing solution that seamlessly bridges the gap between reference management, grant writing, and peer-reviewed manuscript tracking in a unified relational database structure.
opportunities: Build a premium, high-utility 'Academic Research OS' that mimics the actual workflow of a solo laboratory or tenure-track researcher, justifying a premium price tag by saving hundreds of hours of administrative friction.

buyer_persona.team_size: Solo (with occasional management of 1-3 undergraduate or graduate research assistants)
primary_goals: Secure major research funding (e.g., NSF CAREER, NIH R01/R21)
Publish 3-5 high-impact peer-reviewed journal articles per year
Build a cohesive, structured research portfolio for the tenure dossier review
Maintain strict compliance with institutional IRB and safety guidelines
frustrations: Overwhelming administrative burden stealing time from actual research and writing
Difficulty managing the multi-year lifecycle of multiple grants and manuscripts simultaneously
Anxiety over missing compliance deadlines or failing to address peer-reviewer concerns systematically
buying_motivations: The desperate need to save time and reduce cognitive load
The professional necessity of publishing and securing funding to achieve tenure
A desire for a clean, highly functional workspace that matches the intellectual rigor of their research

core_workflows: Literature Mapping and Synthesis (Theme extraction, citation grouping, and gap identification)
Grant Lifecycle Management (Ideation, specific aims drafting, budget tracking, submission, and reporting)
Manuscript Production & Submission (Outline, drafting, internal review, journal submission, and peer-review tracking)
Compliance & Safety Tracking (IRB protocols, biosafety approvals, annual reviews, and amendment submissions)
critical_events: Peer Review Revision Deadlines (typically 30-90 days from decision)
IRB Protocol Expiration and Annual Renewal Deadlines
Annual Faculty Activity Report and Tenure Dossier Submission
recurring_activities: Weekly literature sweeps and systematic reading sessions
Monthly compliance and budget reconciliation audits
business_lifecycle: Phase 1: Conceptualization & Literature Synthesis (identifying gaps in knowledge)
Phase 2: Funding Acquisition (writing and securing grants)
Phase 3: Protocol Approval & Execution (IRB submissions, data gathering, experimentation)
Phase 4: Synthesis & Writing (drafting manuscripts, integrating literature)
Phase 5: Peer Review & Publication (submission, revisions, final publication)
dependencies: Experimental data gathering cannot proceed without approved IRB protocols.
Manuscript writing relies heavily on the Literature Synthesis Matrix.
Grant budget templates must match the funding agency's strict allocation caps.
Resubmissions require addressing 100% of peer-reviewer comments systematically.

core_systems: Literature Synthesis Matrix (Core repository mapping sources to key themes, methodology, and findings)
Manuscript & Publication Pipeline (Kanban tracking of drafts from planning to accepted/published state)
Grant & Funding Engine (Tracker for grant opportunities, specific aims, budgets, and submission milestones)
IRB & Compliance Vault (Repository for tracking protocols, amendments, approval statuses, and renewal dates)
supporting_systems: Research Project Hub (Connecting literature, grants, and manuscripts to specific overarching research questions)
External Collaborator Directory (Tracking co-authors, peer-reviewers, and grant program officers)
Academic Output Dossier (Automated repository collecting published papers, active grants, and service for tenure review)
management_systems: Daily Deep Work Cockpit (Focus dashboard optimized for distraction-free reading, writing, and synthesis)
Academic Administrative Control Center (Task list, institutional meetings, teaching schedule integration)
reporting_systems: Tenure Metric Tracker (Automated dashboard summarizing total publications, impact factors, citations, and active grant funding)
Grant Budget Utilization Report (Tracking allocated vs. spent funds across active research projects)
automation_opportunities: Zotero to Notion sync via third-party integration (e.g., Notion-Zotero) to automatically populate the Literature Synthesis Matrix
Formula-based warning systems alerting 60 days prior to IRB protocol expirations
Automated creation of Peer-Reviewer Response templates upon changing manuscript status to 'Revision Requested'

databases.name: DB_Literature_Library
databases.purpose: Stores and categorizes all read papers, books, and reports; serves as the foundation for the synthesis matrix.

databases.name: DB_Research_Projects
databases.purpose: The high-level container linking specific research questions, active experiments, grants, and manuscripts.

databases.name: DB_Manuscripts
databases.purpose: Tracks all active writing projects, target journals, submission deadlines, and current publishing statuses.

databases.name: DB_Grants_Funding
databases.purpose: Manages the grant pipeline from initial RFP tracking to active funding management and reporting deadlines.

databases.name: DB_IRB_Protocols
databases.purpose: Ensures institutional compliance by tracking protocol approval numbers, expiration dates, and annual renewals.

databases.name: DB_Reviewer_Comments
databases.purpose: Deconstructs peer-review feedback into actionable, line-by-line revision tasks linked to specific manuscripts.

properties: DB_Literature_Library: Citation Key (Text), Publication Year (Number), Authors (Text), Journal (Select), Key Findings (Text), Synthesis Themes (Multi-Select), PDF Link (Url), Research Projects (Relation), Manuscripts (Relation)

DB_Manuscripts: Target Journal (Select), Impact Factor (Number), Submission Deadline (Date), Status (Select: Drafting, Internal Review, Submitted, Under Review, Revision Requested, Accepted, Published), Word Count (Number), Research Projects (Relation), Reviewer Comments (Relation)

DB_Grants_Funding: Funding Agency (Select), Opportunity ID (Text), Budget Requested (Number), Submission Deadline (Date), Status (Select: Ideation, Writing, Submitted, Awarded, Rejected), Specific Aims (Text), Research Projects (Relation)

DB_IRB_Protocols: Protocol Number (Text), Approval Date (Date), Expiration Date (Date), Status (Select: Draft, Under Review, Approved, Expired, Amendment Pending), Renewal Warning (Formula), Research Projects (Relation)
property_types: Relation (connecting all core databases to ensure a unified relational ecosystem)
Formula (for calculating compliance warnings, citation counts, and manuscript turnaround times)
Select/Multi-Select (for rigid categorization of statuses, funding agencies, and synthesis themes)
Date (for tracking strict academic and federal submission deadlines)
relations: DB_Literature_Library is related to DB_Research_Projects and DB_Manuscripts.
DB_Manuscripts is related to DB_Research_Projects and DB_Reviewer_Comments.
rollups: DB_Research_Projects rolls up total funding awarded from DB_Grants_Funding.
DB_Research_Projects rolls up total publications completed from DB_Manuscripts.
DB_Manuscripts rolls up total pending reviewer comments from DB_Reviewer_Comments.
formulas: IRB Days Until Expiration: dateBetween(prop("Expiration Date"), now(), "days")
IRB Renewal Warning: if(prop("IRB Days Until Expiration") <= 0, "🚨 EXPIRED - STOP RESEARCH", if(prop("IRB Days Until Expiration") <= 60, "⚠️ RENEWAL DUE SOON", "✅ Compliant"))
Manuscript Target Progress: format(round(prop("Word Count") / prop("Target Word Count") * 100)) + "% Complete"
views: Literature Library: Synthesis Matrix View (Grouped by Synthesis Themes, displaying Key Findings and Related Manuscripts)
Manuscript Pipeline: Kanban Board (Grouped by publishing status from Ideation to Published)
Grants Tracker: Calendar View (Showing upcoming RFP deadlines and progress report dates)
Compliance: Safety & IRB Board (Displaying active vs. expiring protocols with formula-driven warning indicators)

homepage_structure: Header Section: Dynamic greeting, quick statistics (Active Grants, Manuscripts Under Review, Upcoming Deadlines)
Left Column: Navigation panel, Quick Actions menu, Active IRB Compliance Alert Center
Center Column: The Daily Focus Arena (Dynamic filter showing only research tasks and writing goals for today)
Right Column: Active Research Projects list with progress bars, and upcoming 14-day calendar of academic deadlines
navigation_structure: Primary Hubs: 📚 Literature Synthesis Matrix, ✍️ Manuscript Pipeline, 💵 Grant & Funding Engine, 🛡️ Compliance & IRB Vault
Supporting Dashboards: 📂 Active Research Projects, 👥 Academic Network & Collaborators, 🎓 Tenure Dossier & Metrics
dashboard_hierarchy: Level 1: Academic Research OS Master Cockpit (Strategic Overview)
Level 2: System-Specific Hubs (e.g., Literature Synthesis Matrix, Manuscript Pipeline)
Level 3: Individual Item Pages (e.g., Detailed Manuscript Page with embedded Reviewer Comments Database, or a specific Grant Workspace with embedded budget tracking)
daily_workflow: 1. Open Daily Focus Arena: Review today's writing targets and urgent literature to read.
2. Conduct Deep Work Writing: Draft directly in the Manuscript Pipeline workspace with the Literature Synthesis Matrix opened side-by-side.
3. Log Literature: Import 2-3 new papers, extract key findings, and relate them to active manuscript sections.
weekly_review: 1. Reconcile Grant Budgets: Update spent funds and check upcoming reporting deadlines.
2. Monitor Manuscript Statuses: Update journal response statuses (e.g., check if a paper moved from 'Submitted' to 'Under Review').
3. Review IRB Expirations: Check the compliance status warning system for protocols needing annual renewal.
monthly_review: 1. Update Tenure Dossier Metrics: Document newly published papers, impact factors, and newly awarded grants.
2. Strategic Literature Mapping: Review the Synthesis Matrix to identify new conceptual gaps for future grant proposals.

premium_modules: The Synthesis Matrix Engine: A highly customized relational layout that acts as a structured literature review generator, grouping literature by researcher-defined intellectual themes and linking them directly to manuscript outlines.

The Grant Budget Line-Item Allocator: A dynamic internal database within the Grant Engine that tracks personnel, equipment, travel, and indirect costs (F&A) against the funding agency's strict budget caps.
advanced_dashboards: The Peer-Review Response Command Center: A dedicated dashboard triggered when a manuscript receives a 'Revision Requested' status. It breaks down reviewer letters into actionable rows, letting the scholar track 'Reviewer Comment', 'Planned Revision Action', and 'Manuscript Draft Location' in a side-by-side view.
decision_support_tools: Journal Matcher & Impact Matrix: A tool comparing candidate journals based on Impact Factor, acceptance rates, open-access fees, and average turnaround times to optimize publication strategies.
risk_management_tools: The IRB Compliance Warning System: A automated audit dashboard using complex Notion date formulas to flag expiring protocol approvals, preventing costly research pauses or compliance violations.
profit_optimization_tools: Grant ROI Calculator: Compares the time investment required for a grant proposal against the funding amount and probability of success, outputting an 'Efficiency Score' to help solo PIs prioritize high-yield opportunities.

notion_limitations: Notion does not natively parse PDF annotations or auto-extract metadata from DOI links like Zotero does.
Notion cannot automatically format citations in APA/MLA/Chicago style dynamically based on journal guidelines.
recommended_workarounds: Advise users to use free tools like 'Notion-Zotero' integration to sync library items, or use Web Clipper to import metadata, using custom Notion formulas to concatenate Author, Year, and Journal into a standard citation key.
Provide pre-made formula properties that auto-generate basic APA-style reference strings from the database fields.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Can I import my existing library from Zotero or EndNote?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Yes! While Notion doesn't have a native PDF parser, you can easily sync your Zotero library directly to the ScholarlyOS Literature database using free third-party connectors like Notion-Zotero, preserving all your citation keys and metadata.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Is this template suitable for researchers outside of the USA?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Absolutely. While the system is optimized for US-based academic milestones (such as NIH/NSF grant formats and typical IRB compliance), the underlying databases are highly customizable and can be easily adapted to any country's academic or funding framework.

frequently_asked_questions.question: I am a solo researcher. Is this system too complex for one person?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Not at all. ScholarlyOS is specifically designed to act as a 'virtual research assistant' for solo scholars. It automates the administrative overhead of tracking deadlines and cross-referencing notes, allowing you to focus entirely on your actual research and writing.
